Root.name.notes: Identifies the field on submit and is the key for the Form errors object. Takes precedence over <Field.Control name>.

Root.validate.type: (value: unknown, formValues: Form.Values) => string | string[] | null | void | Promise<...>
Root.validate.notes: Custom validation running after native constraint validation; async supported (but async does not block submission under validationMode='onSubmit').

Item.disabled.notes: Disables the wrapped control; Root disabled wins.

Label.nativeLabel.notes: Set false when the label is not a <label> (e.g. composing over a button trigger) to avoid label behaviour leaking onto buttons.

Error.match.notes: true always shows the message (external control); otherwise matched against ValidityState, e.g. match="valueMissing".

Validity.children.notes: Render-prop-only part exposing validity, errors, value, initialValue, transitionStatus.

dataAttributes: Root/Label/Description/Control/Item/Error: data-disabled, data-valid, data-invalid, data-dirty, data-touched, data-filled, data-focused
Error adds data-starting-style / data-ending-style for its enter/exit animation

renderProp.mechanism: render on every part (Root, Label, Description, Control, Item, Error)
renderProp.elementForm: render={<div />}; the documented group pattern composes Fieldset.Root render={<RadioGroup />} or render={<CheckboxGroup />}

controlled.note: Field.Root itself is uncontrolled: it derives valid/touched/dirty/filled/focused from the registered control unless you override them.

formIntegration.hiddenInput: No hidden input of its own — it registers whatever control is inside; controls that need one (Select, Slider, NumberField, Checkbox...) render it themselves.
formIntegration.validation: Full native constraint-validation integration: required/minLength/maxLength/pattern/step are read from the wrapped control; errors from <Form errors> are merged in and cleared when the value changes; Field.Error with no children displays the native message.

keyboard.keys: None of its own; behaviour comes from the wrapped control.
keyboard.focus: Label click focuses/activates the control; focus state surfaces as data-focused.

notableDifferences: React Aria wraps controls in a single component with props (label, description, errorMessage, isInvalid); Base UI splits them into parts (Root/Label/Description/Error/Control/Validity/Item) that must be composed.
React Aria's isInvalid/isDisabled/isRequired/isReadOnly on the field map to invalid/disabled (+ required on the control) and to data-invalid/data-disabled attributes.

Validation is native-first: Base UI reads the constraint-validation API from the control, whereas React Aria drives validity through isInvalid + validate return values. Async validate is supported here too.
Field.Validity is a render-prop-only part for reading raw validity state; React Aria exposes this through field state objects instead.
Errors can be pushed in from the server via <Form errors={{ fieldName: 'message' }}> and are cleared per-field on change.
